This spec covers four requested changes:

1. Windows named `window1`, `window2`, … must sort numerically, not
   character-by-character (and default names stay un-padded: `window1`,
   **not** `window01`).
2. A new **card view** for tabs alongside the existing detail (table) view,
   with resizable cards (GUI control + hotkeys), a content thumbnail per
   card, and a metadata overlay whose fields and order are configurable in
   Settings.
3. An intuitive UI control to manually rename a window.
4. Single-click on a tab row must **not** navigate to the tab; navigation
   moves to double-click (plus the existing explicit controls).

Issues, ambiguities, and open questions found while analyzing the request
against the current code are collected in
[Issues & open questions](#issues-open-questions) — please review that
section before approving. Per the workflow, a revised version of this spec
would be `…-v002-….qmd`.

## Requirement 1 — Numeric sorting of window names

### Current behavior and root cause

The assumption in the request is correct: window names are compared as
plain lowercase strings in three independent sort sites, so
`window10` sorts between `window1` and `window2`:

- `components/Sidebar.tsx` — `sortedWindows` (the sidebar window list;
  default sort is by name ascending, so this is where the misordering is
  most visible).
- `App.tsx` — `getSortedTabs`, `case 'window'` (the "Window" column sort in
  the All Tabs table).
- `components/TabListView.tsx` — `displayedTabs`, `case 'window'` (the same
  sort duplicated for uncontrolled/AI-group tables).

The name *generator* (`services/nameGenerator.ts`) already produces
un-padded `window1`, `window2`, … — no change there, and **no zero-padding
will be introduced**.

### Design

Add a single shared comparator in a small new module (e.g.
`services/sortUtils.ts`) and use it at all three sites:

```ts
export const compareWindowNames = (a: string, b: string) =>
  a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' });
```

`localeCompare` with `numeric: true` is a *natural sort*: any run of digits
inside a name is compared by numeric value, so
`window1 < window2 < … < window10 < window11`. This satisfies "sort by just
the numerical number" for the default names while also behaving sensibly
for names that are not purely `window<N>`:

- Custom/AI names without digits (e.g. `Research`, `Shopping`) sort
  alphabetically among themselves.
- Mixed sets interleave alphabetically with numeric runs compared
  numerically (`Project 2 < Project 10`).

The duplicated string-compare logic stays where it is (this spec does not
refactor the three sort sites into one), only the comparison for the
window-name field changes.

## Requirement 2 — Card view for tabs

### View toggle

- A **Detail / Card** toggle (two-icon segmented control, e.g. list icon and
  grid icon) is added to the header toolbar next to the existing preview
  toggle.
- The choice persists across sessions (`chrome.storage`, see
  [Persistence](#persistence-settings-schema)).
- The toggle applies everywhere the tab list renders: All Tabs, By Window,
  sidebar-checkbox filtering, and each AI group (each group renders its own
  grid under its heading).
- Search, sorting, checkbox multi-select, selection/preview, keyboard
  navigation, and the close action all keep working in card view; sorting
  controls move into a small sort dropdown in the toolbar when card view is
  active (there are no column headers to click).

### Card layout and grid

- Cards are laid out with CSS grid:
  `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--card-width), 1fr))`
  — they wrap automatically and are responsive to window and pane width.
- Each card represents **one tab** and shows:
  - a **thumbnail** of the tab's page content filling the card (see next
    section), and
  - a **metadata overlay** hovering above the thumbnail (semi-transparent
    scrim, anchored to the bottom of the card) so the user sees both the
    page and the data. Default field order matches the requested priority:
    **icon → last accessed → tab name → domain → window name**.
- If the visible metadata does not fit the overlay, the overlay itself is
  scrollable (`overflow-y: auto` with a max height). Because the browser
  natively scrolls the innermost scrollable element under the pointer, the
  requested hover-governed behavior falls out for free: wheel over a card's
  overlay scrolls that overlay; wheel anywhere else scrolls the main tab
  grid.
- Selected card gets the same indigo ring treatment as a selected row;
  checkbox and close (×) sit in the card's top corners (visible on
  hover/selection, like today's row actions).

### Card sizing

- **GUI control:** a compact slider in the toolbar (visible only in card
  view) plus `−` / `+` stepper buttons, adjusting card width between
  ~160 px and ~480 px in steps. A double-click on the slider handle (or a
  reset button) returns to the default (~240 px).
- **Hotkeys:** `Ctrl` `+` / `Ctrl` `-` (also accepting `Ctrl` `=` for the
  unshifted plus key) grow/shrink cards; `Ctrl` `0` resets. Handled on
  `keydown` with `preventDefault()`, and **only while card view is
  active** — in detail view the browser's normal page-zoom shortcuts are
  untouched. `Ctrl` + mouse wheel over the grid also resizes (optional,
  cheap to add, same guard). See issue 2 below for the zoom-shortcut
  trade-off.
- The chosen size persists across sessions.

### Thumbnails

Chrome gives extensions **no way to screenshot a background tab**
(`chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab` only captures the active tab of a
window). The design therefore reuses the mechanism the Preview Panel
already uses — `getTabContent` in `services/tabService.ts` captures the
page's HTML via `chrome.scripting.executeScript` — rendered small:

- Each card renders the captured HTML in a sandboxed `<iframe srcDoc …>`
  scaled down with `transform: scale(…)` (`pointer-events: none`, same
  `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and injected `<base>` tag as the Preview
  Panel), so the thumbnail is a genuine miniature of the page.
- **Lazy + bounded:** thumbnails are captured only for cards visible in the
  viewport (IntersectionObserver), fetched through a small concurrency
  queue (e.g. 4 at a time), and cached per tab id + URL so re-scrolling and
  re-renders don't re-inject scripts. Off-screen cards drop back to the
  cheap placeholder to bound memory (see issue 3 for scale concerns).
- **Fallbacks:** sleeping (discarded) tabs, restricted pages
  (`chrome://`, Web Store), and capture failures show a placeholder —
  large favicon + domain on a neutral background, with a moon badge for
  sleeping tabs. Card view does **not** auto-wake sleeping tabs (waking
  ~100 tabs to thumbnail them would defeat Chrome's Memory Saver); the
  existing Preview Panel "Wake up & preview" flow remains the way to wake
  a specific tab.

### Metadata configuration (Settings)

- The Settings (gear) menu gains a **"Card view options"** section listing
  the five fields — icon, last accessed, tab name, domain, window — each
  with a visibility checkbox (easy on/off) and up/down reorder arrows (or
  drag handles).
- The order also controls truncation priority: fields render in order and
  the overlay scrolls when they overflow, so higher-priority fields are the
  ones visible without scrolling.
- Configuration persists across sessions.

### Persistence (settings schema)

`StorageData` in `types.ts` (and `services/storageService.ts`) gains:

```ts
tabViewMode?: 'detail' | 'card';        // default 'detail'
cardWidth?: number;                     // px, default 240
cardMetadata?: { field: 'icon' | 'lastAccessed' | 'title' | 'domain' | 'window';
                 visible: boolean }[];  // default: all visible, order as above
```

## Requirement 3 — Manual window rename

**This already exists**, though it is evidently not discoverable enough:
in the sidebar, **double-clicking a window name** opens an inline edit
box, and hovering a window row reveals a **pencil (✎) icon** that does the
same. Enter saves, Escape cancels, renames persist to storage and
participate in the existing undo/redo history. (The interactive tour
mentions the double-click, but nothing in the resting UI advertises it.)

Proposed discoverability improvements (rather than a new mechanism):

- Make the pencil icon on sidebar rows **always visible** (subtle, not
  hover-only) so the affordance is self-evident.
- Add the same inline rename to the **main content header**: when viewing a
  single window (By Window mode), the window-name `<h1>` gets a pencil
  button and double-click-to-edit, wired to the same `handleRenameWindow`
  path.

If something else was intended here (e.g. rename from the card/detail view
rows, or a right-click context menu), see issue 5.

## Requirement 4 — Single click must not navigate

### Current behavior

In `components/TabListView.tsx` a row click runs
`onSelect(tab.id); onActivate(tab);` — i.e. every single click both selects
the row *and* switches Chrome to that tab, which yanks focus away from the
dashboard.

### Design

- **Single click** — selects the row/card only (highlights it and shows it
  in the Preview Panel). No navigation.
- **Double click** — navigates (activates) the tab. Applies to both detail
  rows and cards.
- Unchanged explicit navigation affordances (so the feature stays
  discoverable): the **↗ Switch to Tab** hover button on each row/card, the
  **Enter** key on the keyboard-selected tab, and the ↗ button in the
  Preview Panel header.
- Copy that teaches the old behavior gets updated: the extension info
  banner and tour/user-guide text will mention "double-click (or ↗ / Enter)
  to switch to a tab".

## Issues & open questions {#issues-open-questions}

1. **Spec file naming deviates from the documented convention.** The
   request asked for `SPEC-4.0.3-v001-someMeaningfulName.qmd` (the version
   was later bumped to 4.0.4 — see issue 9), but
   `docs/spec-conventions.qmd` defines
   `SPEC-<version>-<Description>-v<NNN>.qmd` (revision *last*), which the
   three existing 4.0.2 specs follow. This file follows the request as
   given. Please confirm which format wins; if the new one, the conventions
   page and (optionally) the old filenames should be updated for
   consistency.
2. **`Ctrl` `+` / `Ctrl` `-` shadow browser zoom.** Chrome delivers these
   keydowns to the page and honors `preventDefault()`, so the hotkeys are
   implementable — but while the dashboard is focused **in card view** the
   user loses keyboard page-zoom (mitigations: hotkeys only active in card
   view; `Ctrl` `0` still resets card size; browser zoom remains available
   via the Chrome menu). If that trade-off is unwanted, alternatives are
   `Ctrl` `Shift` `+`/`-` or `[` / `]`.
3. **Thumbnails cannot be true screenshots, and scale is a real concern.**
   Screenshot APIs only work for the active tab, so thumbnails are
   scaled-down HTML captures (same source as the Preview Panel). Two
   consequences: (a) JS-heavy pages may look imperfect in miniature
   (already true of the Preview Panel); (b) with ~170 tabs, hundreds of
   live iframes would be heavy, hence the lazy-render / concurrency-queue /
   off-screen-eviction design. If in practice this is still too heavy, the
   v002 fallback is favicon+domain placeholder cards with thumbnails only
   for the hovered/selected card.
4. **"Each card should show a view of the contents of the window"** — this
   spec interprets a card as representing **one tab** (mirroring the detail
   rows and the metadata list you gave, which is per-tab), with the
   thumbnail showing that tab's page. If you instead wanted one card per
   *browser window* (a window's tabs summarized inside a card), that is a
   different layout — say so and v002 will respec it.
5. **Rename already exists** (sidebar double-click + hover pencil). This
   spec assumes the ask is really about discoverability and adds the
   affordances in Requirement 3. If you wanted a different control (context
   menu, rename button in the toolbar, rename from tab rows), flag it for
   v002.
6. **Keyboard navigation in the card grid.** Today `←`/`→` switch focus
   between sidebar and tab list, and `↑`/`↓` move through tabs. In a grid,
   users expect arrows to move in two dimensions, which collides with the
   sidebar-switch binding. Proposed for v001: keep `←`/`→` as area
   switching, and have `↑`/`↓` step linearly through cards (previous/next
   in sort order). If you want true 2-D grid navigation, we'd move area
   switching to `Tab` or `Ctrl` `←`/`→` — preference?
7. **Numeric sort with custom names.** "Sort by just the number" is
   well-defined for `window<N>` names but not for renamed windows
   (`Research`, `Shopping`). The natural-sort comparator handles both
   (numbers numeric, text alphabetic); confirm that is acceptable rather
   than, say, forcing number-less names to the end.
8. **Double-click reachability.** Double-click as the sole *click*
   navigation is fine on desktop, but it is slower for rapid tab hopping
   and unfriendly to some accessibility setups — which is why the ↗ button
   and Enter remain first-class. No action needed; noting the reasoning.
9. **Tag/version mismatch.** Per instruction, the latest commit
   (`c72a0a1`) is tagged `v4.0.3`, but `package.json` and `manifest.json`
   at that commit still say `4.0.2` (no 4.0.3 version-bump commit was ever
   made). Harmless, but worth knowing; the first commit of this work should
   bump both files straight to `4.0.4`.

## Affected files (planned)

- `services/sortUtils.ts` — **new**: shared natural-sort comparator.
- `components/Sidebar.tsx` — numeric name sort; always-visible rename
  pencil.
- `App.tsx` — numeric sort in `getSortedTabs`; view-mode/card-size/metadata
  state + persistence; sizing hotkeys; header rename affordance; toolbar
  toggle, slider, and card-view sort dropdown; updated banner copy.
- `components/TabListView.tsx` — numeric sort; row click = select only,
  double-click = activate.
- `components/TabCardView.tsx` — **new**: card grid, thumbnail iframes,
  metadata overlay, lazy capture queue.
- `components/CardViewOptions.tsx` (or inline in the settings menu) —
  **new**: field visibility/order editor.
- `services/tabService.ts` — thumbnail capture reuse (cache + concurrency
  around `getTabContent`).
- `services/storageService.ts`, `types.ts` — new persisted settings.
- `components/OnboardingTour.tsx` / tour copy in `App.tsx`,
  `components/UserGuideModal.tsx` — updated click-behavior wording.
- `_quarto.yml` — this spec added to the book.
- `package.json`, `manifest.json` — version bump to 4.0.4 (see issue 9).

## Out of scope

- True pixel screenshots of background tabs (not possible with current
  Chrome extension APIs without focusing each tab).
- Auto-waking sleeping tabs to capture thumbnails.
- Card view for the *windows* list in the sidebar (see issue 4 — only if
  requested in v002).
- Refactoring the three duplicated sort implementations into one (only the
  comparator is shared).
